stem:
a. CRT monitors are being replaced by LCD monitors in homes and offices. Give THREE reasons. (3 marks)

b. Name TWO operating systems other than Windows. (2 marks)
answer:
a. LCD monitors are thinner/lighter, normally consume less power and produce less heat than comparable CRT displays. Each is a distinct practical advantage.

b. Linux and macOS (other valid examples include Android and FreeBSD).
better:
Better responses depicted good understanding of CRT and LCD monitors and they justified the statement given in the question with valid reasons, for instance: LCD has better quality (resolution) of image than CRT monitor; LCD occupies less space than CRT monitor; LCD can be easily mounted on the wall than CRT monitor; LCD allows connectivity of external devices such as flash drive but CRT does not provide such connectivity; LCD provides more interactive interface than CRT; LCD weighs less than CRT monitor.

Better responses showed a good basic knowledge about the operating systems and listed names of the two operating systems, other than Windows, correctly. They listed names such as: UNIX; LINUX; DOS (Disk Operating System); iOS.
weaker: Weaker responses did not understand the demand of the question and failed to list the names of operating systems other than Windows. They listed names such as: compiler; interpreter; batch-operating system; real-time operating system; Windows XP; BIOS; system software; application software.

stem:
a. Identify each printer characteristic as dot matrix or laser. (2 marks)

| No. | Characteristic |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Uses paper with holes along both sides for feeding |
| 2 | Non-impact printing |
| 3 | Page-based printing |
| 4 | Low-quality output at a slow print rate |

b. State true/false and show working for each statement. No marks without working. (3 marks)

1. A 4 GB flash drive can store 130 sound files of 50 MB each.
2. An 8 megabit/s link transfers 10 MB in 10 seconds.
3. A 1.5 TB hard disk has 1500000 MB capacity.
answer:
a. 1: Dot matrix; 2: Laser; 3: Laser; 4: Dot matrix (the conventional printer types in the paper).

b. Using decimal SI units consistently:

1. False: 130 × 50 MB = 6500 MB = 6.5 GB, greater than 4 GB.
2. True under the ideal no-overhead assumption: 10 MB × 8 = 80 Mb; 80 Mb ÷ 8 Mb/s = 10 s.
3. True: 1.5 TB × 1000000 MB/TB = 1500000 MB.

Convention note: the source examples mix decimal and binary conversion conventions. Under binary-sized equivalents, 4 GiB is 4096 MiB, the second transfer is 10.48576 s if MB means MiB but link rate is decimal, and 1.5 TiB is 1572864 MiB. State the convention rather than mixing factors.
better:
Better responses showed in-depth understanding of the dot matrix and laser printers and identified the given characteristics correctly. These responses identified the first and fourth characteristics in the table as the characteristics of the dot matrix printer and the second and third characteristics in the table as the characteristics of the laser printer.

Better responses demonstrated good understanding of conversion amongst the memory units. The candidates applied the concepts on each given problem to determine whether it is true or false and showed its working.
weaker:
Weaker responses mostly depicted confusion between the characteristics of two printers and identified the characteristics of dot matrix printer as that of laser printer and vice versa. Some of these responses marked the symbols of tick and cross instead of writing the name of printer in front of characteristics given in the question that shows the lack of understanding of the question.

Weaker responses failed to show the correct working to determine true and false statements. Most of these responses showed confusion amongst the conversion of memory units such as 1024 bytes = 1030 gigabytes, 1024 bytes = 1040 terabytes, 1 gigabyte = 102 and 1 terabyte = 105.

stem: Describe FIVE advantages of setting up a computer network in an office.
answer:
1. Share printers/storage to reduce duplicated equipment.
2. Share authorised files and collaborate on common documents.
3. Communicate through email or internal messaging.
4. Centrally administer user permissions and software.
5. Centrally back up shared data and simplify recovery.

These are advantages of connecting computers; security and reliable backup still require proper configuration.
better: Better responses depicted a good understanding of the advantages of computer networks. The advantages written by these responses included: sharing peripheral devices; file sharing; cheaper software licenses for computer networks rather than for individuals; easy monitoring of work; data centeralisation; centralised management of network; easy backup and recovery; cost effective; fast retrieval of information; easy access to files and folders on other computers.

stem: Differentiate LAN and WAN on speed, security, setup cost, coverage area and transmission errors.
answer:
| Feature | Typical LAN | Typical WAN |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Speed | Often high local bandwidth and low latency | Performance depends on provider, link and distance; typically greater latency |
| Security | Usually one organisation administers local access | Crosses wider/shared infrastructure; needs suitable authentication and encryption |
| Setup cost | Usually lower within one site | Usually higher for connecting dispersed sites and leased/provider links |
| Coverage | Room, building or campus | Cities, countries or wider geographic regions |
| Transmission errors | Short controlled links may face fewer impairments | Longer/more complex paths can face more impairments; actual error rate depends on link technology |

These are conventional comparisons, not absolute laws. A well-engineered WAN can be fast and secure, and a misconfigured LAN can be insecure.
better: Better responses revealed that the candidates had good conceptual knowledge of the differences between LAN and WAN. Features written by these responses to differentiate between LAN and WAN included: speed is high in LAN and low in WAN; security is less in LAN and more in WAN; setup cost is low in LAN and high in WAN; coverage area is small in LAN and large in WAN; transmission errors are few in LAN and more in WAN.
weaker: Weaker responses mostly, differentiated between LAN and WAN on the basis of speed and coverage area correctly but failed to differentiate on the basis of security, setup cost and transmission errors.

stem: Define bandwidth, modulation, guided media, baseband signal, serial transmission and synchronous transmission.
answer:
- Bandwidth: in the question’s networking usage, maximum data-transfer capacity, measured in bits per second; analogue frequency bandwidth is measured in hertz.
- Modulation: varying a carrier property such as amplitude, frequency or phase according to information.
- Guided media: physical transmission paths such as twisted pair, coaxial cable and optical fibre.
- Baseband signal: the original/unshifted information signal; baseband transmission sends it without translating it to a higher-frequency carrier.
- Serial transmission: sending the bits of a data stream sequentially on a channel.
- Synchronous transmission: coordinated timing permits reception of a continuous stream or framed blocks without separate start/stop bits for each character.
better: Better responses showed a good basic knowledge about the terminologies of computer networks. Definitions written by these responses included such as: Bandwidth is maximum capacity of a link to transfer data/ data transferring speed; Modulation is the process of imposing input signal on the carrier signal/ the process of converting digital signal into analog signal, guided media refers to the transfer of data via cable or physical path from sender to receiver; Baseband is original frequency range of a transmission signal/ it consists of frequencies that are near to zero/ low bandwidth signal/ signals sent by telegraph; Serial transmission is bit by bit transmission of data is called serial transmission; Synchronous transmission is a data transfer method in which continuous stream of signals is sent along with timing signals (clock signals)/ data is sent in the form of packets or blocks with clock signal.
weaker: Weaker responses depicted poor knowledge about the terminologies of data transmission and defined the terms given in the question incorrectly. These responses included such as: Bandwidth sends and receives data in a network/ type of transmission through wired medium; Modulation transfers data to the application software/ it is the encryption process; Guided media sends and receives information and data/ guided media is where data is guided; Baseband signal controls the signals and transmits data/ a signal that is sent through a single wire; Serial transmission transmits data in a line/ used for long distance transmission; Synchronous transmission converts data into useful information/ data is transmitted with start and stop bit in synchronous transmission.

stem:
Ahmed uses the keyboard in Word. Text box A contains upright “I love Pakistan”; B contains italic “I Love Pakistan”. Give shortcuts to:

a. Make A match B. (1 mark)
b. Change B’s font size from 15 to 11. (1 mark)
c. Underline B’s text. (1 mark)
d. Restore accidentally deleted text. (1 mark)
answer:
Select the intended text before applying formatting.

a. `Ctrl+I` toggles italics and matches the intended visual difference. The source also changes lowercase love to Love; `Ctrl+I` does not change that spelling/capitalisation, which needs a separate edit if an exact text match is required.
b. `Ctrl+Shift+P`, type 11, Enter sets the exact size. Alternatively press `Ctrl+[` four times to decrease 15 → 14 → 13 → 12 → 11. The official single `Ctrl+[` reduces by only one point and does not alone reach 11.
c. `Ctrl+U` toggles underlining.
d. `Ctrl+Z` undoes the deletion, assuming it is the most recent action.

Write Excel functions with ranges to calculate:
a. Total participants.
b. Average age.
c. Youngest age.
d. Number qualified MA.
e. Number aged at least 30.
(1 mark each)
answer:
a.
```text
=COUNTA(A3:A9)
```
Result: 7. COUNT(A3:A9), printed in the source commentary, does not count these text names. COUNT(D3:D9) is also valid here because every participant has a numeric age.

b.
```text
=AVERAGE(D3:D9)
```
Result: 29.

c.
```text
=MIN(D3:D9)
```
Result: 26.

d.
```text
=COUNTIF(E3:E9,"MA")
```
Result: 5.

e.
```text
=COUNTIF(D3:D9,">=30")
```
Result: 3. The official commentary’s COUNT(D3:D9,">=30") does not apply a condition and is incorrect.

stem:
i. Complete the blank block diagram, using these term numbers: 1 Control unit; 2 Memory unit; 3 ALU; 4 Register; 5 Input unit; 6 Output unit. Solid lines show data flow and dashed lines show control. (5 marks)

ii. Give TWO differences between RAM and ROM. (2 marks)

iii. Explain the data, address and control buses. (3 marks)
answer:
i. Diagram positions: upper-left 5 (Input), upper-middle 2 (Memory), upper-right 6 (Output), centre 3 (ALU), bottom 1 (Control). Term 4 (Register) is unused in the five-box diagram.

ii. RAM is normally read/write volatile working memory; ROM retains data without power and normally holds persistent firmware that is not changed during routine execution. Both can be read; EEPROM/flash-based firmware can be updated using appropriate procedures.

iii. Data bus carries data/instructions between components; address bus carries the address of the memory or I/O location to access; control bus carries operation/timing/status signals such as read, write and interrupts. A bus transports signals; it does not itself store data.
better: Better responses showed that candidates had a good understanding of the block diagram of a computer system and completed the diagram by writing the correct term numbers in the relevant boxes. Likewise, these responses differentiated RAM and ROM correctly. For instance, these responses included: RAM is temporary memory while ROM is permanent memory; RAM stores data until power is supplied while ROM retains data even if power supply is off; RAM is volatile memory while ROM is non-volatile memory. Similarly, these responses depicted strong understanding of the different types of buses and described the purpose of each bus correctly. These responses included: data bus carries data signal; it connects CPU, memory, input and output devices; address bus carries memory address signals; it connects CPU and memory only; control bus carries signals from the control unit to other units; control bus carries signals to control activities of all units.
weaker: Weaker responses depicted poor understanding of the block diagram of a computer system. Some of these responses managed to identify the input and output blocks but were unable to identify other blocks. Likewise, these responses mostly managed to write one difference between RAM and ROM, i.e. RAM is a temporary memory and ROM is a permanent memory. However, second difference written by the candidates included: RAM stores less amount of data than ROM; RAM stores recently performed tasks while ROM stores complete files; RAM can only be accessed by programs while ROM can be accessed by only persons. Similarly, these responses managed to write the purpose of data bus but showed lack of understanding about control bus and address bus. These responses included: control bus specifies the path for data to flow; control bus manages most of the CPU commands; each component in computer has its own address and address bus stores that address; data bus stores the memory that is used by CPU; control bus is used to control signals and transfers data from memory to CPU; address bus stores their ID and send and receive data.

stem:
i. Describe SIX different computer crimes. (6 marks)

ii. List FOUR data-protection rules to keep data safe. (4 marks)
answer:
i. Examples:

1. Unauthorised access: entering a computer/account without permission.
2. Phishing: deceptive messages/sites used to steal credentials or information.
3. Deliberate malware distribution: deploying malicious software to damage or compromise systems.
4. Data theft: taking confidential records without authorisation.
5. Software piracy: unauthorised copying/distribution that infringes software copyright.
6. Online fraud: using computer systems to deceive others into giving up money or assets.

ii. Apply least-privilege access and strong unique passwords with MFA; patch supported operating systems/apps; maintain tested backups with an offline/protected copy; use updated anti-malware and avoid untrusted downloads/attachments.

The question asks for six crimes and four protections. Examples of harmful conduct should not be confused with legitimate defensive tools. Password changes are warranted after compromise; forced frequent changes alone do not replace strong unique credentials.
better:
Better responses revealed that candidates had good understanding of computer crimes. Most of these responses described hacking, phishing, software piracy, information theft, plagiarism, transmitting computer viruses, cyber bulling and pharming.

Better responses showed that the candidates struggled to write exact data protection rules and mostly wrote measures to protect data such as: the firewall should be used to protect network data; password should be changed frequently; update software frequently; data must be store in a backup; install antivirus and update it regularly; install licensed software because unlicensed software may steal your data; avoid opening spam email; use biometric verification to login to system; avoid connecting external hard drives and flash drives to your system.
weaker:
Weaker responses showed that candidates had lack of understanding of the computer crimes and described irrelevant terms rather than computer crimes. These responses described encryption, debugging, addiction of internet, copyrights, client-server overuse and hard disk loading.

Weaker responses mostly mentioned either non-tech security steps or incorrect rules. These responses included: data can be protected by errors; data is protected by eye witness; use personal security to secure data; do not share personal information with anyone; avoid using copyrighted software because they authorise a user to get your personal data; do not download copyrighted software because it brings virus in computer.
